title: Illustrative: agency PO matching for translator invoices
statement: Although freelance translators already use generic invoicing tools, matching invoices to agency purchase orders and chasing agency payment terms remains manual, because generic tools do not model per-word rates, PO numbers or agency payment portals. This matters because late agency payments are the most frequently reported cash-flow pain in this illustrative evidence set.

picos.population: Freelance translators who bill translation agencies (segment S-AGENCY-TRANSLATORS)
picos.intervention: Invoicing with purchase-order matching and agency payment-term reminders
picos.comparator: Generic invoicing SaaS (dom:example.com), suite billing modules (dom:example.org), spreadsheets and manual reminder emails
outcomes: Minimize the time it takes to match an invoice to an agency purchase order
Minimize the number of agency invoices paid after the agreed term
picos.setting: Solo freelancers in Europe and North America invoicing in several currencies

why_empty: Illustrative example only: the segment is small for horizontal invoicing vendors, and translation-management suites bill on behalf of agencies rather than serving the freelancers who invoice them.

assumptions.text: Agency-billed translators lose at least an hour per month matching invoices to purchase orders.
assumptions.riskiest_test: Problem interviews with 10 agency-billed translators (Mom Test)

assumptions.text: Translators will pay at least 9 USD per month for automatic purchase-order matching and agency reminders.
assumptions.riskiest_test: Van Westendorp pricing survey on the waitlist

assumptions.text: Agency purchase orders can be parsed reliably from the PDFs and emails translators already receive.
assumptions.riskiest_test: Parse 30 real purchase-order samples provided by interviewees

reduce: setup steps before the first invoice
